texts.preamble: Zydus Wellness Limited vs Union Territory Of J And K And Anr on 27 December, 2024 Author: Sanjay Dhar Bench: Sanjay Dhar In The High Court Of Jammu & Kashmir And Ladakh At Srinagar Crm(M) 4/2020 CrlM(4/2020) Zydus Wellness Limited ...Petitioner(s Through: Mr. Varut Kumar Gupta, Advocate Vs. Union Territory Of J And K And Anr. ...Re (Health And Medical Education Department) Through: Mr. Mubashir Majid Malik, Dy. Ag Mr. Zahid Qais Noor, Ga Coram: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Sanjay Dhar, Judge Order
texts.facts: The petitioner has challenged the proceedings emanating against him on a complaint filed by the respondents alleging commission of offences under Section 26(2) (ii) of Food Safety and Standards Act 2006, hereinafter referred to as FSS Act-2006, punishable under Section 51 & 59 (I) of FSS Act-2006 which is stated to be pending before the Court of learned Judicial Magistrate 1st Class (Munsiff ) Qazigund. 02. It is alleged in the impugned compliant that on 11.03.2024 complainant- Food Safety Officer, Qazigund, during the routine inspection visited the premises of accused No.1-Tawkeer Ahmad Khanday (Food Business Operator) situated at Qazigund. The complainant is stated to have collected the sample of a food article namely "Yummy Nutrilite Spread" and after completing the requisite formalities the sample was sent for analysis to the Food Analyst Kashmir. Vide report dated 26.03.2014, the Food Analyst, Kashmir declared the sample as of Standard quality. However, the Designated Officer Food Zydus Wellness Limited vs Union Territory Of J And K And Anr on 27 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183626945/ 1 Safety Anantnag decided to send --2-- the 2nd part of the sample to the Referral Laboratory at Kolkata for its comprehensive analysis. The Director Food Referral laboratory, Kolkata vide its report dated 11.07.2014 declared the sample as Unsafe and Sub- Standard quality. 03. During investigation of the case, accused Tawkeer Ahmad Khanday was found to be the Proprietor of M/s: Khanday Kiryana Merchants, Qazigund, where from the sample of 'Nutralite Yummy Spread" was procured for analysis and it was found that he had purchased the said food item from Parvaiz Ahmad Sheikh who in turn had purchased the food item in question from M/s: MSK Traders Tangbagh Khayam Srinagar. It was also found that that MSK Traders, Srinagar had purchased the said food item from M/s: Vee Ess Agencies Gandhi Nagar Jammu (C & F Agent of Zydus Wellness Ltd.), and it was further found that label of the food item was bearing the address and name of petitioner's company. 04. The Designated Officer submitted the case to the Commissioner of Food Safety, J&K for grant of sanction of prosecution vide his letter dated 27- 08-2014 for obtaining sanction of prosecution against the accused Tawkeer Ahmad Khanday, Parvaiz Ahmad Sheikh, Mubashir Ahmad Khan, Prop. of M/s VEE ESS Agencies Gandhinagar, Jammu and the petitioner herein i.e., M/s: Zydus Wellness Ltd. Vide Order No.04-CFS of 2015 dated 21-11-2015, the Commissioner of Food Safety accorded sanction for launching prosecution against the above-named persons including petitioner herein. Accordingly, the complaint was presented before the learned Judicial Magistrate 1st Class (Munsiff ) Qazigund on --3-- on 09.02.2016, on which date cognizance was taken and the process was issued against the accused persons including the petitioner herein. 05. The petitioner has challenged the impugned complaint and the order whereby the process has been issued against it, primarily, on the ground, that the complaint has been filed beyond the prescribed period of limitation and as such, it was not open to the learned trial Magistrate to take cognizance of offences and issue process against the accused. It has also been contended that the order whereby cognizance of offences has been taken and process was issued against the petitioner is mechanical in nature. 07. As per the complaint the sample of Food Article in question was collected by Food Safety Officer on 11.03.2014 where after it was sent to the Food Analyst. The Food analyst rendered his report dated 26.03.2014, whereafter the Designated Officer sent the sample to the Director Food Zydus Wellness Limited vs Union Territory Of J And K And Anr on 27 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183626945/ 2 Laboratory Kolkata for re-analysis . The report of re- analysis which forms basis of the complaint was rendered by the said laboratory on 11.07.2014. The sanction for prosecution was granted on 21.11.2015 and the complaint was filed before the learned Judicial Magistrate 1st Class (Munsiff) on 09.02.2016.
texts.arguments: It reads as under: "77. -Notwithstanding anything contained in this Act, no court shall take cognizance of an --4-- offence under this Act after the expiry of the period of one year from the date of commission of an offence: Provided that the Commissioner of Food Safety may, for reasons to be recorded in writing, approve prosecution within an extended period of up to three years." 08. 10. Learned counsel for the respondents has vehemently argued that once the Commissioner of Food Safety has granted sanction for prosecution in terms of order dated 21.11.2015 it has to be presumed that he has extended the period for launching the prosecution.
